_comment: 1. Many robots stand around the notebook, and the robot that arrives last
cannot: NO_SPACE_AROUND_TARGET, naming the robots in the way.
Round 1 sends twelve robots to notebook.n.01_1, which is four teams'
worth. Its standable ring holds about six -- bodies and
DestinationRegistry reservations alike, at 1.24 m separation (open defect
7) -- and the notebook is a small object on the floor of a small room, so
the ring is tighter than a piece of furniture's and fills sooner.
The four drones do not compete for it: bodies more than LAYER_SEPARATION_Z
(0.6 m) apart in z are different layers, and a Crazyflie hovers at 1.2 m.
So the eight ground robots are the ones contending.
ridgeback_5 is the designated victim and is the point of the file. It sets
off 240 ticks after the rest -- two seconds of playback, since the
recorder captures every 4th tick at 30 fps -- and that is enough twice
over: the twelve travel 6.8-8.7 m at 10 ticks/m, so they are all standing
(or refused) by about tick 150. Then it navigates, in round 2, and is
refused with the blockers named.
